effects: The reward owner's claimed counter rises by _rewardAmount, which uses up that much of their claimable validator reward (reverts if it goes over the total awarded).
When _wrap is false, _rewardAmount of native FLR is sent from the reward manager to _recipient.
When _wrap is true, _rewardAmount of FLR is deposited into WNat for _recipient, so _recipient receives WFLR, not FLR.
The function is not payable, so the signer sends no native value.
The caller must be the reward owner or one of its executors; an executor can only pay to the owner or to an allowed recipient.
formats.shown: "Claim/Wrap Reward" with the reward owner, the recipient, the amount as FLR and a raw Wrap true/false flag.

findings.title: claim: when wrap is true the recipient gets WFLR, but the amount reads as native FLR.
findings.evidence: GenericRewardManager._sendWrappedRewardTo: `wNat.depositTo{value: _rewardAmount}(_recipient);`. Case 0 (wrap=true) shows 'Reward Amount: 1 FLR' with only 'Wrap: true' to say the asset is WFLR.
findings.fix: Rename the Wrap field, e.g. 'Receive as WFLR (wrapped)', and add an interpolatedIntent that names the wrap, so the asset that arrives is clear.

findings.title: claim: the _wrap flag is shown as a raw true/false, with no meaning attached.
findings.evidence: descriptor field `#._wrap` 'Wrap' format 'raw'. Cases 0 and 3 show 'Wrap: true' / 'Wrap: false'.
findings.fix: Use a clearer label such as 'Receive wrapped WFLR instead of FLR'.

findings.title: claim: the intent 'Claim/Wrap Reward' does not say which action happens, how much, or to whom.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent like 'Claim {_rewardAmount} reward of {_rewardOwner} to {_recipient} (wrap: {_wrap})'.

findings.title: claim: the recipient and owner address types are limited to eoa/wallet, but the code accepts any address.
findings.evidence: descriptor params types ["eoa","wallet"] on `#._recipient` and `#._rewardOwner`. GenericRewardManager.claim takes any `address payable _recipient`.
findings.fix: Drop the types restriction or add 'contract'.

effects: Removes every executor the signer set before.
Lets each listed address call claim for the signer's rewards at any time, paying them to the signer or to the signer's allowed recipients.
An empty list revokes all executors.
formats.shown: "set executors" with each new executor address listed.

findings.title: setClaimExecutors: the intent 'set executors' does not say executors can claim the signer's rewards.
findings.evidence: GenericRewardManager.setClaimExecutors: `claimExecutorSet[msg.sender].replaceAll(_executors);` with _checkOnlyOwnerOrExecutor letting them call claim. Descriptor intent "set executors".
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Authorize addresses to claim your validator rewards (replaces existing list)' and label the field 'Authorized claimer'.

findings.title: setClaimExecutors: the call replaces the whole executor list, and an empty list revokes all, but the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: AddressSet.replaceAll calls clear(_state) then addAll. The intent only says 'set executors'.
findings.fix: Mention 'replaces all current executors' in the intent.

findings.title: setClaimExecutors: case 1 gives the executor the address-book name 'Reward Owner', a confusing fixture.
findings.fix: Use a separate executor address in the test.

effects: Removes every allowed claim recipient the signer set before.
Lets the signer's executors send the signer's rewards to any listed address (the signer itself is always allowed).
An empty list leaves only the signer as an allowed recipient for executors.
formats.shown: "set recipients" with each new recipient address listed.

findings.title: setAllowedClaimRecipients: the intent 'set recipients' does not say executors can then send the signer's rewards there.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Allow executors to send your rewards to these addresses (replaces existing list)'.

findings.title: setAllowedClaimRecipients: the call replaces the whole recipient list, which the screen does not say.

couldNotCheck: WNat.depositTo (the wrapped FLR contract that claim calls when _wrap is true) has no source in the directory. I assumed it mints WFLR to _recipient one-for-one.
